discovery: Atom interferometry: the realization of matter-wave interferometers with atoms and their development into precision sensors

nominees.name: Jürgen Mlynek
nominees.affiliation: University of Konstanz / Humboldt University Berlin (emeritus), Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: In 1991 three experiments turned de Broglie waves of whole atoms into working interferometers: Mlynek's double-slit with helium, Pritchard's nanofabricated-grating interferometer with sodium, and Kasevich's light-pulse interferometer with laser-cooled atoms. Pritchard used it for the first measurements of atomic polarizability and coherence with matter waves. Kasevich turned light pulses into beam splitters, giving gravimeters, gradiometers and gyroscopes of unprecedented sensitivity. Atom interferometry now measures the fine-structure constant at the 0.1 ppb level, gives precise values of Newton's G, tests the equivalence principle, constrains dark energy and dark-sector forces, and is the basis for planned gravitational-wave and dark-matter detectors. It is used on drones, ships and in space. Few new instruments have opened so much fundamental physics to laboratory tests while also yielding practical inertial navigation and geophysics. This is a new measurement capability in the tradition the Prize honours.
